javax.microedition.broadcast
Interface ServiceContextListener

public interface ServiceContextListener

ServiceContextListener defines the interface to listen to events from a ServiceContext.

Implementations use constants specified here to post the events. Applications can test the event by using "==" operator instead of String.equals() method.

Field Detail

COMPONENTS_IDENTIFIED

static final java.lang.String COMPONENTS_IDENTIFIED
Posted when all the components are identified by acquiring information related to the selected service. By default, some of these components are selected for presentation.

This event entails an array containing the ServiceComponents selected for presentation. Thus the third argument to contextUpdate(ServiceContext,String, Object) is never null, and must be cast to ServiceComponent[]. If there is no component contained in a selected service, an array of zero-length is given. To affect the default selection of service components, listeners may invoke setComponents.

Note that only after all listeners get notified of this event and complete their execution, the ServiceContext is moved to PREPARING_MEDIA state.

See Also:
Constant Field Values

COMPONENTS_SET

static final java.lang.String COMPONENTS_SET
Posted when a set of components in a selected service is set for presentation. This event passes to the registered listeners a relevant reason code as the third argument to contextUpdate(ServiceContext,String,Object). The argument is never null. The list of ServiceComponents set may be obtained with ServiceContext.getSelectedComponents().

See Also:
Constant Field Values

CONTEXT_CLOSED

static final java.lang.String CONTEXT_CLOSED
Posted when the associated context has been closed.

This event entails no additional information. Thus the third argument to contextUpdate(ServiceContext,String,Object) is always null.

See Also:
Constant Field Values

CONTEXT_STOPPED

static final java.lang.String CONTEXT_STOPPED
Notified when the current presentation of a service has been stopped.

This event entails a reason code. Thus a listener may compare the third argument to contextUpdate(ServiceContext, String,Object) with reason codes defined in this interface. The argument is never null.

See Also:
Constant Field Values

PLAYERS_REALIZED

static final java.lang.String PLAYERS_REALIZED
Notified when all the media controlled using MMAPI are prepared for presentation. This event passes to the registered listeners an array of Players newly created for presentation. When there is no Player created, this event is not generated. Once posted, all listeners must get notified and fully complete before starting the Players.

In the case of component changes, if there is a Player sharing the time base with the newly added components, then the Player's state will just be updated without affecting its current state. In this case, no new Player will be created and the Player shall not show up in the list passed to the listeners.

The third argument to contextUpdate(ServiceContext,String,Object) is never null, and must be cast to Player[]. Since this event is delivered only when there is at least one newly created Player. The argument always contains at least one Player.

The Players are all in the Player.REALIZED state, so the application may obtain the appropriate Controls from those Players.

In the case of videos, VideoControls can be obtained and javax.microedition.media.control.VideoControl#initDisplayMode(int,Object) may be invoked to configure the presentation of videos. Note that those Players are automatically started after a delivery of this event.

See Also:
Constant Field Values

PRESENTATION_STARTED

static final java.lang.String PRESENTATION_STARTED
Posted when Players responsible for the presentation of selected service components are fully started. This event entails no additional information. Thus the third argument to contextUpdate(ServiceContext,String,Object) is always null.

See Also:
Constant Field Values

REASON_ALTERNATIVE_CONTENT

static final java.lang.String REASON_ALTERNATIVE_CONTENT
Alternative content is presented in place of the normal, designated content (a reason code). This reason code may be specified in the following circumstances:
  • The previous selection caused a selection of an alternative content, which may be a separate service or a set of components. Such an alternative content includes the purchase dialog or advertising content for the actual service that was requested.
  • During the presentation of a service, an event with this reason code is generated if any of the service components being presented are replaced by alternative content. Such an example includes the expiration of a free preview period.

See Also:
SELECTION_INITIATED, COMPONENTS_SET, Constant Field Values

REASON_EQUIVALENT_SERVICE

static final java.lang.String REASON_EQUIVALENT_SERVICE
The current service delivered on one broadcast bearer is being replaced by another bearer delivering the equivalent service (a reason code).

This may happen during a handoff from one broadcast bearer to another due to problems with radio signal coverage of the first bearer, for example.

See Also:

REASON_NO_RIGHT

See Also:

REASON_NORMAL_CONTENT

static final java.lang.String REASON_NORMAL_CONTENT
The currently presented alternative content has been replaced by the normal, designated content (a reason code). An event with this reason code is generated in the following circumstance:

During the presentation of a service, an event with this reason code is generated if an alternative content was being replaced by the normal, designated content of the selected service. For example, such an event may be generated when an end user completes a pay-per-view dialog. As the result, the advertising content will be replaced by the original content of service.

See Also:

SELECTION_INITIATED

static final java.lang.String SELECTION_INITIATED
Posted when a selection to a service has been initiated. This is normally initiated by a call to ServiceContext.select(Service). But in some circumstances, it may be automatically initiated, for example, by the expiration of a free preview period of the current service.

Upon delivery of this event, ServiceContext.getService() returns the service for which the selection is initiated.

This event entails a reason code. The third argument to contextUpdate(ServiceContext,String,Object) is never null, and can be compared with the reason codes defined in this interface.

See Also:

Method Detail

contextUpdate

void contextUpdate(ServiceContext context,
                   java.lang.String event,
                   java.lang.Object data)
Called when there is a change in the ServiceContext.

Parameters:
context - The ServiceContext where an update has occurred.
event - The event code as defined in this interface.
data - The data associated with the event. The type and semantics of this data is documented per each event.
